statement.p: Evaluate the integral \int\!\!\!\int_R (x^{2}-2y^{2}) \, dA, where R is the first quadrant region between the circles of radius 1 and radius 4 centred at the origin.

static.solution: \int_R (x^{2}-2y^{2}) dA = \int_0^{\pi/2} \int_{1}^{4} r^2(\cos^2\theta - 2\sin^2\theta)r\,dr\,d\theta. Evaluating the inner integral, we have \int_R (x^{2}-2y^{2}) dA = \int_0^{\pi/2} (\cos^2\theta-2\sin^2\theta)\cdot\frac 1 4 r^4 \bigg|_{1}^{4} \, d\theta = \frac14 \int_0^{\pi/2} (\cos^2\theta-2\sin^2\theta)\cdot(255)\,d\theta. So \int_R (x^{2}-2y^{2}) dA = \frac{255}{4} \int_0^{\pi/2}(\cos^2\theta-2\sin^2\theta)\,d\theta = \frac{255}{4} \int_0^{\pi/2} -\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos 2\theta\,d\theta = \frac{255}{4} \cdot (-\frac{1}{2}\,\theta) + (\frac{3}{2})(\frac12)\sin2\theta \bigg|_0^{\pi/2} = -\frac{255\pi}{16}.
